title: PROMYS Europe
aliases: Program in Mathematics for Young Scientists Europe
organizer: PROMYS Europe (partnership of PROMYS, Wadham College Oxford, the Mathematical Institute at the University of Oxford, and the Clay Mathematics Institute)
host_institution: Wadham College, University of Oxford, United Kingdom

proposed_updates.citizenship_restrictions: Students must be 'ordinarily resident in Europe' -- the program's own definition explicitly includes 'all countries adjacent to the Mediterranean.' Türkiye is Mediterranean-adjacent, so a Türkiye-resident high schooler is squarely inside the stated eligible population, not merely an unaddressed edge case.
proposed_updates.cost_currency_note: GBP, not USD. GBP 4,200 for the 2026 cycle covers tuition, accommodation, and all meals -- officially stated to represent less than half the programme's true per-participant cost. Full or partial financial aid (including 100% aid plus travel costs) is explicitly available to families tax-resident in Europe (same Mediterranean-adjacent definition), so cost is not a hard barrier for a qualifying Turkish family.
proposed_updates.current_cycle_label: 2026 first-year applicant closing date was 8 March 2026 -- already elapsed as of this research (2026-08-26). Decisions were released on a rolling basis 14-22 April 2026. Next (2027) cycle's deadline not yet published.

turkey_access_reasoning: This is one of the cleanest possible Turkey-eligibility findings this session: the program's own eligibility text names 'Mediterranean-adjacent' countries as explicitly included in its definition of Europe, and Türkiye is unambiguously Mediterranean-adjacent. This is a real distinguishing fact -- PROMYS Europe is Oxford-hosted intensive mathematics coursework (guided problem sets and number theory, in the same pedagogical model as PROMYS US), genuinely distinct from PROMYS US (already live in the DB) by location, institution, and specific eligible population, not a yearly-cycle duplicate of the same program.

evidence.quote: Students must be ordinarily resident in Europe; we include in this all countries adjacent to the Mediterranean.

The standard fee for students for PROMYS Europe 2026 is £4200. This fee covers tuition, accommodation and all meals...Full or partial financial aid is available for those who would otherwise be unable to attend...Students may apply for financial aid if their families are tax residents in Europe (including the UK and all countries adjacent to the Mediterranean). For those receiving full financial aid, all charges are waived and the programme also covers travel costs.

notes: Discovered via seed PDF '2. Highly Competitive Summer Programs' (row 'PROMYS (Program in Mathematics for Young Scientists) Europe'). Confirmed via SQL that only US-based 'PROMYS (Program in Mathematics for Young Scientists)' exists in the live DB -- PROMYS Europe is genuinely absent and genuinely distinct (different host country/institution/eligible-population), not a duplicate.
